page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized server within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier (top 10%) performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench text processing. Conversely, multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores, align with the average (middle 50%) tier. Memory read and write bandwidth, Passmark memory scores, and Redis SET operations also perform within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the server provides a cost-efficient allocation of memory relative to compute cores. However, the 1 GB NVMe SSD local storage is a notable tradeoff, restricting local data persistence and requiring external storage attachments for most database applications. In terms of machine learning workloads, the server exhibits a weak (bottom 25%) result for LLM prompt processing on medium (7B) models, though it reaches the top tier (top 10%) for text generation on small (135M) models.

The Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is suited for memory-bound workloads that do not demand extensive local storage. Appropriate use cases include in-memory caching, text processing pipelines, single-threaded data compression tasks, and lightweight web serving.
